$comment: The expo-updates fingerprints of the binaries currently in users' hands.
An `eas update` only reaches a build whose fingerprint matches exactly;
publishing to any other value reports success and reaches zero devices,
with no error anywhere. scripts/verify-ota-target.mjs compares the working
tree against this file and refuses to publish on a mismatch.
Update this file in the same commit that ships a new binary, and never to
silence the preflight — a mismatch means the update cannot land, not that
"setAside" lists files that landed on main after that binary was built and
only touch another platform's native code. scripts/publish-ota.mjs removes
them from its throwaway tree before fingerprinting that platform, so JS from
main still reaches the binary. Drop the list when that platform ships a new
binary. This file is not a fingerprint input, so editing it never moves one.
